stories.summary: Google on Wednesday unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model, stepping up competition with OpenAI and Anthropic as the race to build more capable coding and cybersecurity systems intensifies. Google says Carbon delivers state-of-the-art performance on cybersecurity tasks including vulnerability discovery, exploitation and patching, and generates secure code at more than twice the success rate of Gemini 4 Argon on internal benchmarks. Carbon is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and is first being made available to a subset of cybersecurity defenders through Google's Fairwind Program while safeguards are tested.
stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon, a cybersecurity-focused frontier model

stories.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing is the biggest story of Wednesday, October 28, with the company listing in its own words that its AI could blackmail people, become sentient or even end humanity, alongside explosive growth figures. Reuters' market coverage notes Anthropic filed for a US IPO on Monday and that the offering could value the company at a record-breaking $1.5 trillion or more. The filing names only OpenAI and Google as direct frontier-model competitors, underscoring how concentrated the top of the market has become.
stories.title: Anthropic IPO filing lays out AI risks and a possible $1.5T valuation

stories.summary: Google DeepMind showed Genie 4 on October 27, a world model that builds interactive scenes in real time and is the first real-time world model to generate audio natively, with ambient sound and characters that talk and react to the user. Users can change a scene with plain text, and Gemini 3.8 Flash acts as a guiding agent that splits goals into steps and adjusts the plan as the user intervenes. Genie 4 is a research preview for trusted testers, with Google AI Ultra subscribers set to get it in Project Genie.
stories.title: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, a real-time world model with sound

stories.summary: Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey unveiled Dessa on October 24, a new AI voice tool from Block that talks, laughs, pauses and interrupts like a person, with Dorsey posting on X that talking with it feels like talking with a person. His post gained over 13 million views over the weekend, with reactions ranging from people asking when it will be available to others calling it dystopian. Dessa is not public yet, with Block giving early access to a small group of AI safety researchers and no release date announced.
stories.title: Jack Dorsey's Dessa voice AI, which laughs like a human, goes viral on X

stories.summary: OpenAI added iCloud Mail and Calendar plugin support to ChatGPT on October 27, announcing the update in a post on X and calling the plugins much requested. Apple users can now link their email and calendar to the chatbot, asking it to find a specific email, catch up on the inbox, check what is next on the schedule or update a calendar event. The plugins work on all ChatGPT plans and are available on web, desktop and iOS.
stories.title: ChatGPT adds iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins

stories.summary: Oracle says Google's TPUs will reach its cloud in 2027, the first hyperscale cloud outside Google to offer them, and The Information reports OpenAI plans to buy the chips too. The shift gives Nvidia a real rival for rented compute, with more places to run models on non-Nvidia chips putting pressure on what users pay per token, though not before 2027. The move matters for anyone training or serving models whose stack is tied to Nvidia's software.
stories.title: Oracle to rent Google TPUs in 2027 as OpenAI reportedly buys in
